commentary:
Energy is the morning's story, and it's doing the heavy lifting for the whole risk tone. Brent and WTI dropped more than 2% — Brent back below $98 — after Shell's CEO said Middle East oil flows have recovered to roughly 80% of pre-war levels, and the curve is confirming the supply-normalisation narrative: Brent's prompt spread has slumped to its weakest backwardation in over a month, puts dominate the options tape, and open interest sits at its lowest since March 2025. The products complex is unwinding even harder, with heating oil off 3.4% and gasoil down 4.2% despite the structural tight-refining story keeping diesel cracks elevated into 2027, according to reports.

That oil slide is easing inflation nerves and feeding straight into rates and risk. Treasuries rallied across the curve with the long end leading (Ultras +0.55%), gold reversed early losses to trade near $4,190 as rate-trajectory fears cooled, and equity index futures pushed higher globally — S&P eyeing its first record since August, Euro Stoxx up 0.7%. Note the French angle: OAT futures jumped nearly 1% and euro bank shares rallied 1.6% after Le Pen pledged to court bond investors with deficit cuts toward 3%. The dollar's recent resilience remains a rate-differential story, and if markets pare back the hikes currently priced, that gap narrows — watch this week's Fed minutes and Treasury auctions as the test.

In ags, the wheat complex firmed (KC +1%), soybean meal rose 1.3%, and OJ spiked nearly 7%, while cocoa pulled back from its El Niño-driven run as West African supply risk gets repriced.
